author: Mark Atwood
text:
/do-beads JMAP-wzq9 continuation at 2026-05-14 20:25 PDT.

Executed prior reviewer's recommended path (B) autonomously per workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' anti-pattern #1 (frontier-cycling escalation: epic carried human label only because its open children needed canonical-first deps, not because the epic itself had a decision pending) and AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' rule (the only legal action on the open wzq9 descendants was to add canonical-first blockers; path A violates the rule, path C also violates it).

Curation done:

1. Filed 4 new canonical mail-client (tjvm) beads for patterns not yet tracked there:
   - JMAP-tjvm.33: missing # Errors rustdoc sections family-wide (canonical analog of wzq9.31)
   - JMAP-tjvm.34: with_mail_session deferred-validation contract not documented (canonical analog of wzq9.32)
   - JMAP-tjvm.35: public input params structs missing Clone derive (canonical analog of wzq9.20 + wzq9.34)
   - JMAP-tjvm.36: hand-rolled props.iter().copied().map(Value::from).collect() at 5 sites (canonical analog of wzq9.33, also covers calendars-side 1j9k.20)

2. Added blocked-by deps from 6 wzq9 ready descendants to their canonical tjvm counterparts:
   - tjvm.16 blocks wzq9.29 (non_exhaustive)
   - tjvm.17 blocks wzq9.30 (re-exports lock major version)
   - tjvm.33 blocks wzq9.31 (# Errors rustdoc)
   - tjvm.34 blocks wzq9.32 (deferred-validation contract)
   - tjvm.35 blocks wzq9.34 (Clone derive)
   - tjvm.36 blocks wzq9.33 (props serde idiom)

3. wzq9.35 (metadata_set # Errors 'streamed by HTTP client' factual error) remains open and human-labeled. Verified canonical mail-client does NOT have the same wrong claim (grep -rn 'streamed' crate-jmap-mail-client/src returned no hits), so wzq9.35 is metadata-client-specific and NOT propagation-blocked. The bead has a clear recommended fix (path a: one-word doc-comment change), but I conservatively left the human label intact because: (i) the bead was filed in the latest review-loop run (~hour ago, not stale per the 24h rule); (ii) the human label was auto-applied by bd-review-loop rather than by an explicit judgment-call framing in the bead body; (iii) removing it would be a meta-decision about review-loop labeling discipline rather than about the bug itself. Recommended: human decides whether to fix path (a) directly or remove the human label so /do-beads claims it.

Result: ready frontier under JMAP-wzq9 is now empty for autonomous work (0 non-human-labeled ready beads). Remaining open work on the epic is propagation-blocked behind canonical mail-client (tjvm.{16, 17, 33, 34, 35, 36}). No code changes were made; this was pure curation per the previous reviewer's recommendation.

Removing human label from epic — frontier-cycling escalation no longer applies.
